text.p: CanWest Global Communications Corp Chief Executive Officer Israel Asper said on Thursday he expects the broadcast company will see a "substantial advance" in profits, dividends and developments in 1997.

Asper, who is also chairman, told shareholders at the annual meeting that CanWest, which in 1996 posted record net earnings of C$102 million after discontinued operations, expects to hit new records this year. "Our recently completed year established new highs, new records and new challenges...and outlook for fiscal 1997 convinces us that past records will be exceeded again this year," he said.

Asper told the meeting CanWest Global will continue to expand in New Zealand and Australia. "Our development efforts in New Zealand will see us acquiring the remaining 50 percent of TV3 in 1997, as well as launching a new major market network, TV4."
Also, Asper said he anticipates that Australian investors will ultimately be able to snap up the company's 76 percent economic interest in Australia's Network Ten.

Asper said he was still determined to advance CanWest's holdings in a bid to become Canada's third national television network. On Tuesday the Canadian government denied a CanWest appeal to overturn an earlier decision denying it a television broadcasting license in Alberta.

"We will never rest until we have expanded our operations in Canada and have achieved fully national operational status, by reaching into Alberta and Quebec in a much more meaningful way than we do now," Asper said.

Canada's Heritage Minister Sheila Copps said on Tuesday that the government agreed with CanWest the possibility of a third coast-to-coast network should be examined. Currently Canada has the Canadian Broadcasting Corp and CTV Television Network Ltd, among whose shareholders are Baton Broadcasting Inc and WIC Western International Communications Ltd.
